title: ChatGPT for Good? On Opportunities and Challenges of Large Language Models for Education
extended_summary:
This position paper examines the opportunities and challenges of large language models, especially ChatGPT/GPT-3-like systems, for education. The authors focus on how these models could support learning and teaching through content generation, personalized feedback, lesson planning, assessment support, and educational dialogue, while also identifying major risks such as bias, hallucinations/unverified output, overreliance by learners and teachers, copyright/plagiarism issues, privacy and security concerns, and sustainability costs.

The paper is not an empirical intervention study; instead, it synthesizes existing literature and proposes a conceptual view of how large language models may be integrated into educational settings. It discusses applications across learners and teachers in primary, secondary, tertiary, and professional development contexts, and briefly references use cases such as quiz generation, feedback generation, adaptive tutoring, and teacher support for lesson design and grading.

The main conclusion is that large language models can be valuable educational tools, but only if they are used with human oversight, critical thinking, fact-checking, clear governance, and strong privacy and ethical safeguards. The authors argue that educational systems need training, policies, and responsible design approaches to prevent misuse, protect student data, reduce bias, and ensure that the technology complements rather than replaces human instruction.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's generative AI chatbot and large language model system for dialogue, text generation, and assistance across tasks.
identified_tools.use_case: Discussed as a general-purpose large language model for education, including teacher lesson planning, personalized feedback, assessment, and professional development; no empirical evaluation in this paper.

quality_tier_rationale: This is a position paper and literature discussion, not an empirical evaluation of a tool. It provides conceptual opportunities and risks rather than a study with a clear methodology or measured outcomes.
impact_tier_rationale: No direct effect sizes, samples, or outcome measurements are reported for an intervention. The paper identifies possible benefits and harms, but does not demonstrate impact empirically.
